findings.location: Sec. 1, para 'The 2026 situation': "is disputed~\cite{Constantin2026c,Bastounis2026}"
findings.problem:
Misattributed citation: neither cited paper disputes the scope of OpenAI's result relative to Fefferman's problem statement.
- Bastounis–Circelli–Hansen argue that the Lean proof does not correspond to the natural-language proof, through mismatched intermediate lemmas. They do not discuss the forced/unforced scope, and note 03 records that they do not claim the headline theorem is wrong.
- Constantin–Ignatova–Vicol prove a conditional regularity result: constructions with OpenAI's features (i) and (ii) cannot have a real-analytic force. That is a technical limitation of the method, not a dispute about Fefferman's statement.
- The scope dispute is documented in press: SciAm, 21 Sep 2026 (library key Howlett2026b).
findings.evidence:
- arXiv API, 2610.08144 abstract: "we show that the formalised Lean proof does not correspond to the NL proof". It says nothing about scope or forcing.
- arXiv API, 2609.20803 abstract: "the force can neither vanish identically near the singular point, nor be real analytic".
- library/notes/03-openai-navier-stokes-method.md:636: "they do not claim the NL proof or the headline Lean theorem is wrong".
- https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/did-openai-solve-the-wrong-navier-stokes-problem/ (Howlett, 21 Sep 2026) is the article that frames the scope dispute. It also reports CIV's result.
- library/references.bib has the entry Howlett2026b. make_refs.py picks up any newly cited library key automatically.

findings.location: Table 1, row 'Lattice mass gap': "Proved only at strong coupling ... or for finite groups"
findings.problem:
The row is overbroad and, as worded, false. Lattice mass gaps are also proved at weak coupling for continuous groups in lower dimensions:
- 3D U(1) (Villain action) is gapped and confined at all couplings (Göpfert–Mack, which the paper itself cites in Sec. 5 as Gopfert1982).
- In d=2, every lattice gauge theory is gapped and has an area law.
The cited works (Osterwalder1978, Seiler1982, Shen2023, Adhikari2025) support only the 4D statement for continuous non-Abelian G. The library notes say so explicitly, so the row also contradicts them.
findings.fix: 4D lattice mass gap, continuous non-Abelian $G$ & Proved only at strong coupling~\cite{Osterwalder1978,Seiler1982,Shen2023}; never in the weak-coupling continuum regime. (Finite $G$: gap at weak coupling~\cite{Adhikari2025}; 3D $U(1)$: gap and confinement at all couplings~\cite{Gopfert1982}.) \\

findings.location: Sec. 4.1: "This follows the mechanical-verification-first approach advocated in~\cite{Mei2026}."
findings.problem:
This mischaracterizes both the source and the method.
- Mei and Douglas propose combining LLM semantic review with mechanical numerical checks and mechanical vacuity checks. They argue that LLM judges miss errors these mechanical checks catch. They do not advocate a 'mechanical-verification-first' ordering.
- The review in this paper is LLM reviewers followed by LLM verifiers, i.e. the LLM-judge pattern that Mei and Douglas go beyond. Its only mechanical element is the compiling of exploit files. It runs no numerical or automated vacuity scan.
- The review workflow script never references Mei2026, so 'follows' implies a derivation that is not documented.
findings.fix: Compiling exploits in Lean, together with the non-vacuity witnesses of Section~\ref{sec:checked}, is in the spirit of the mechanical vacuity checks of Mei and Douglas~\cite{Mei2026}. They combine LLM-based semantic review with mechanical numerical and vacuity checks, and report that LLM judges miss errors those checks catch. Our verification of findings, by contrast, was LLM-judged.

result.checked:
Read-only review of <repo-root>/paper/main.tex (I checked the flagged phrases against the built main.pdf), set against OS.lean, Lattice.lean, Statement.lean and OpenProblems.lean, library note 01 (sections 2.4-2.9), notes 05, 08 and 09, PROBLEM.md, PLAN.md and critique-mass-gap.md. I also ran the Lean axiom audit: every proved theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and the five open items also depend on sorryAx. That matches the paper.

Checked and correct (with the derivations I redid):
(1) The OS E0-E4 description, the OS I Lemma 8.8 error, and the E0' formula.
(2) The reflection-positivity form, including the field-index factor rho(theta). On the lattice, F_{0i} changes sign under the reflection, so each time index gives a factor -1, which matches theta⊗theta⊗theta⊗theta. One subscript typo is listed below.
(3) The cluster axiom, and the a=0 collapse argument: exact factorization gives B_T≡0, so the Hilbert space is CΩ and NonTrivial cannot hold.
(4) The mass-gap Proposition is correct. B_T(F,G)=<(1-P)F^,(1-P)G^>, e^{-tH} commutes with P, a bound on a dense subset extends to the operator norm, and the spectral theorem finishes it. Vacuum uniqueness is a consequence, not an extra hypothesis. H>=0 and the semigroup come from reconstruction (E0', E1, E2). The step that needs justifying is density; see below. m<infinity does follow from NonTrivial.
(5) Wilson action: with U_p≈exp(i a^2 g0 F), beta(1-(1/N)Re tr U_p)≈a^4 tr F_{μν}^2 when beta=2N/g0^2. Summing gives (1/4)∫F^aF^a. The lattice field strength is ≈ a^2 g0 F, and (U-U†)/2i is already Hermitian.
(6) b0=11N/(3(4π)^2) and b1=34N^2/(3(4π)^4) are right for beta(g)=μdg/dμ=-b0g^3-b1g^5. The asymptotic-scaling expression converges: from aΛ=(b0g^2)^{-b1/(2b0^2)}e^{-1/(2b0g^2)}, 1/g0^2 = 2b0 log(1/a) + (b1/b0) log log(1/a) + const + o(1).
(7) ShortDistanceAF: g^2≈1/(2b0 log(μ/Λ)) and the log^{-2} power are right. Θ is renormalization-group invariant, and two-loop corrections only multiply by (1+O(loglog/log)). The scalar direction v lies in TFFSpace, is O(4)-invariant, and contracts to 2 tr F_{μν}F_{μν} ∝ F^aF^a ∝ Θ. The λ^8 log^2 scaling with D_λ is consistent, and free gluons are excluded.
(8) The 21-dimensional decomposition (0,0)+(0,0)+(1,1)+(2,0)+(0,2) is correct.
(9) The OS1-failure argument in note 01 is correct, and in fact more robust than its premise. A cleaner proof: the Cauchy estimate gives E[φ(g_ε)^2]=O(ε^{8/p})≤O(ε^4). Cauchy-Schwarz with a translate h of g, plus the separated-point asymptotics, gives E[φ(g_ε)^2] ≳ log^{-2}(1/ε). So OS1 fails for any field of scaling dimension >2, and in particular for any theory satisfying ShortDistanceAF. The paper drops the hedge (see findings).
(10) The O(4) obstruction reduction is correct when the other links are frozen to the identity. The plaquette is Q_yQ_x^{-1}, Re tr = 2 q_x·q_y, the weight is exp(beta Σ q_x·q_y), and ordering at large beta is the Fröhlich-Simon-Spencer result. The paper's hedge is adequate (even conservative), but its wording is imprecise.
(11) The claims that periodic limits can be mixtures and that cluster is equivalent to a unique vacuum are right in substance, but the wording needs fixing.

No critical (false) mathematical claim found. One claim is materially overstated (the φ^4_4 statement); the rest are hedging and precision fixes.

findings.location: Sec. 5 (Research landscape), Constructive QFT bullet: "Triviality of $\varphi^4_4$ ... shows that non-triviality in four dimensions requires asymptotic freedom"
findings.problem: Materially overstated. Aizenman–Duminil-Copin prove marginal triviality of the scaling limits of critical 4D Ising and single-component nearest-neighbour lattice φ^4_4 models. They prove nothing about 4D theories in general. That non-triviality in 4D requires asymptotic freedom is a heuristic, not a theorem.
findings.evidence: library/notes/08-constructive-qft-and-renormalization-tools.md:28 calls AF "the only *known* route to a non-trivial 4D continuum limit [H: strongly supported, not a theorem]". The same line has a verifier note that ADC does not cover n≥2 components at large coupling. refs.bib:521 gives the title as 'Marginal triviality of the scaling limits of critical 4D Ising and φ^4_4 models'. note 09:160 has the same scope.

With the perturbative evidence, this supports, but does not prove, the expectation that a non-trivial four-dimensional theory must be asymptotically free.

findings.location: Sec. 2.2 "their regularity axiom fails for dimension-four composite fields such as $\tr F^2$"; Table 2 row "OS1 fails for $\tr F^2$ in 4D"
findings.problem: The math is correct and robust: OS1 fails for any measure-defined field of scaling dimension >2. But the paper states it unhedged, while note 01 labels it an in-house derived claim whose YM premise is heuristic, and it has no published source. In Table 2, 'equivalent to OS' is also a confusing direction label: E0' is OS II's own condition.

findings.location: Sec. 3.3, Proposition proof sketch: "Reconstruction maps ordered-positive $F$ to a dense set of vectors"; Sec. 7 Limitations
findings.problem: The Proposition is correct. Vacuum uniqueness and H≥0 are not missing hypotheses: uniqueness is a conclusion, and H≥0 comes from reconstruction. Three gaps remain. (a) The density of slab-product vectors in the OS Hilbert space, and the equivalence of slab-product reflection positivity with OS's E2 on S_+, are asserted without justification. Both are open, unformalized obligations in PROBLEM.md, and so is this Proposition. The Limitations section omits all of them, although Sec. 3.1/3.2 assert that OS II reconstruction applies. (b) 'The Hamiltonian' means the one on the OS space generated by the 21 fields. (c) Lorentz covariance is not needed for JW's spectral condition on H; it is needed only for the mass-shell form (note 01, Prop. A).

findings.location: Sec. 6.2, Track E: "a slab of $SU(2)$ links with the other links frozen reduces to the 3D $O(4)$ model, which orders"
findings.problem: The reduction is exact only for the time-like links of a height-one slab, with every other link frozen to the identity (or to a pure-gauge configuration). With generic frozen links you get an O(4) model in an SO(4) background, which can be frustrated. The 3D O(4) model orders only for beta above about 0.94; it is rigorous at large beta by Fröhlich–Simon–Spencer. The argument concerns conditional measures under special boundary conditions and implies no bulk transition; the paper should say so, to avoid echoing Grady's disputed claim. The 'heuristic' hedge itself is adequate and conservative (the critique calls it rigorous up to the constant).
findings.evidence: plan/critique-mass-gap.md:118-127: "Freeze every other link to I ... U_p=Q_xQ_y^{-1} ... 3D O(4) model at β_O(4)=β_LQCD ... transition at β_O(4)≈0.936 ... O1 concerns conditional measures on thin sets, not the bulk. It does not imply a bulk transition." My check: Re tr(Q_xQ_y^{-1})=2q_x·q_y, so the conditional weight is exp(β Σ q_x·q_y) for S=βΣ(1-½Re tr U_p).
findings.fix: "A finite-size criterion that is uniform over all volumes and boundary conditions cannot hold in four dimensions beyond bare coupling of order one. Take the time-like $SU(2)$ links of a height-one slab and freeze all other links to the identity. The conditional measure is then exactly the 3D $O(4)$ model at the same $\beta$, which has long-range order for large $\beta$ (numerically for $\beta\gtrsim0.94$, i.e.\ $g_0^2\lesssim4.3$). This is our own unrefereed argument, not a theorem. It concerns conditional measures and implies no bulk phase transition. It directs any certificate approach to cube-restricted criteria."

findings.location: Sec. 4.2, Minor: documentation: "any non-trivial limit forces $\|Z_k\|\sim a_k^{-4}g_0^{-2}$"
findings.problem: This is stated as forced, but it is a perturbative heuristic and depends on the channel. The trace-anomaly scalar (g_0^2 F^2 is RG-invariant) needs Z~a^{-4} without g_0^{-2}; that is exactly what ShortDistanceAF's log^{-2} requires, since a^{-4}g_0^{-2} would make that channel diverge like log^2(1/a). The stress-tensor channel needs ~a^{-4}g_0^{-2}, and the (2,0)+(0,2) channels carry anomalous dimensions. The Lean documentation hedges 'up to logarithms', and g_0^{-2}~log(1/a) is itself such a logarithm.
findings.evidence: Lattice.lean header: "a non-trivial limit forces ‖Z_k‖ → ∞ like a_k⁻⁴ g₀⁻² up to logarithms (anomalous dimensions)". Derivation: T_lat≈a^4 tr F_geo^2, and <ΘΘ>~ḡ^4(1/|x|)|x|^{-8}, so Z_scalar~a^{-4}; for the stress tensor T_can=g_0^{-2}F_geoF_geo, so Z~a^{-4}g_0^{-2}.
findings.fix: \item \textbf{Minor: documentation.} The renormalization matrices were described as ``finite''. Any non-trivial limit is expected to need $\|Z_k\|\to\infty$, like $a_k^{-4}$ times channel-dependent powers of $\log(1/a_k)$ (perturbatively $a_k^{-4}$ for the trace-anomaly scalar and $a_k^{-4}g_0^{-2}$ for the stress tensor).

findings.location: Sec. 3.6, Milestone ladder: "Because \lean{IsWilsonLimit} uses periodic tori, the cluster property amounts to uniqueness of the vacuum"
findings.problem: The causal claim is wrong. Given the other OS axioms, cluster is equivalent to a unique vacuum in general (OS I/II); periodic tori have nothing to do with that equivalence. The periodic-torus point is different: IsWilsonLimit allows no boundary condition, so the periodic limit itself must have a unique vacuum, and no pure phase can be selected.
findings.evidence: library/notes/01-problem-definition.md:93 ("R6 holds iff the vacuum is unique") and :112 ("with E4, also R6"). PLAN.md:81-83.
findings.fix: "Given the other axioms, the cluster property is equivalent to uniqueness of the vacuum. Since \lean{IsWilsonLimit} uses periodic tori with no boundary conditions, this means the periodic limit itself must have a unique vacuum."

findings.location: Sec. 6.1: "limits of periodic tori are in general mixtures whose ergodic components are not themselves periodic limits"
findings.problem: Overstated. Periodic limits can be non-extremal mixtures (for example the low-temperature Ising model), and then their components need not be periodic limits. They are not mixtures 'in general', and for 4D Yang–Mills a unique vacuum is expected. The point is only that this is unproven.
findings.evidence: plan/critique-constructive-qft.md:111 ("If the vacuum is not unique, S fails Cluster ... every periodic subsequence gives ½(μ⁺+μ⁻)").
findings.fix: "The cluster clause requires vacuum uniqueness for periodic limits. Limits of periodic tori can be non-trivial mixtures (as for the low-temperature Ising model, where every periodic limit is $\tfrac12(\mu^++\mu^-)$), and the ergodic components of such a mixture need not be periodic limits. Ruling this out needs infrared input."

findings.location: §10 Data and code availability: "Third-party PDFs are not redistributed."; dev/workflows/*.js
findings.problem:
Two package risks.
- The claim holds only if the deposit is built from Git. The working tree still holds 121 third-party arXiv PDFs in library/pdfs (about 100 MB; arXiv's default licence does not let third parties redistribute them), plus LaTeX build logs. .gitignore excludes them, but a zip of the folder uploaded straight to Zenodo would include them. Zenodo records cannot normally be altered after publication.
- The workflow scripts embed absolute local paths containing the macOS username. This is a low-risk privacy and hygiene issue.
INDEX.md also links to pdfs/ files that will not be in the deposit.
findings.fix: Add to §10: "The Zenodo archive is built from the tagged Git commit (\lean{git archive}) and excludes the local PDF cache, which \lean{scripts/fetch_pdfs.sh} rebuilds." In dev/workflows/*.js, replace '<repo-root>' with a repository-relative root (e.g. process.env.YM_ROOT || '.').
